An ablation applicator for use with a device that ablates tissue in a blood vessel includes a tubular body that forms an internal lumen into which an ablation medium can be delivered. The applicator also has a control mechanism configured to change the tubular body between two states: a passive operating state for introducing the applicator into the blood vessel, and an active operating state for ablating the vessel tissue.  

An ablation medium supply line is provided to feed the ablation medium into the internal lumen. This supply line is located within the lumen and includes multiple apertures through which the ablation medium can flow from the supply line into the lumen, allowing the medium to make thermal contact with the tubular body. At least a portion of these apertures are arranged along the supply line at predefined intervals between adjacent apertures.  

The ablation device may also include a first temperature sensor disposed inside the internal lumen, as well as an ablation medium return line positioned within the tubular body and made of a material that determines the applicator’s active configuration.
outputs.L3:
The ablation applicator is configured for ablating tissue within a blood vessel. It includes a tubular body having an inner lumen through which an ablation medium can be conducted. During use, the tubular body is introduced into the blood vessel and positioned at the treatment site so that thermal energy from the ablation medium can be transferred through the tubular body to the surrounding vessel tissue.

The applicator further includes a control mechanism that allows the tubular body to be converted between two operating states: a passive insertion mode and an active ablation mode. In the passive insertion mode, the tubular body may assume a configuration suitable for atraumatic introduction and advancement through the vessel. In the active ablation mode, the tubular body is changed into a configuration suitable for delivering ablation energy to the targeted tissue region.

An ablation medium supply line is arranged within the inner lumen of the tubular body. The supply line is configured to deliver the ablation medium to the tubular body. To distribute the ablation medium within the inner lumen, the supply line includes a plurality of openings. These openings allow the ablation medium to exit the supply line and enter the inner lumen, where it thermally contacts the tubular body. As a result, heat or cold from the ablation medium can be transferred to the tubular body and then to the adjacent tissue to perform the ablation.

The ablation device may also include a temperature sensor positioned inside the inner lumen. The temperature sensor can be used to monitor the temperature of the ablation medium, the tubular body, or the treatment environment during operation. In addition, the device may include a return line formed from a material that defines or helps define the active shape of the applicator. This return line may assist in removing the ablation medium from the inner lumen while also contributing to the structural configuration of the tubular body when the applicator is placed in the active ablation mode.
outputs.L4:
An ablation applicator for treating blood vessel tissue is designed to deliver controlled thermal energy to a target vascular region while allowing the device to be introduced, positioned, and activated in a reliable manner. The applicator includes an elongate tubular body having an inner lumen extending through at least a portion of its length. The tubular body is dimensioned for insertion into or alongside a blood vessel and is configured to support the delivery of an ablation medium, such as a heated or cooled fluid, to tissue that is to be treated.

A control mechanism is coupled to the tubular body and is operable to switch the applicator between at least two functional states. In an insertion mode, the applicator is configured to assume a condition suitable for advancement through tissue or through a vascular pathway. This may include a relatively low-profile, flexible, or atraumatic configuration that facilitates placement at the desired treatment location. In an ablation mode, the applicator is configured to promote effective transfer of thermal energy from the ablation medium to the surrounding blood vessel tissue. The control mechanism may mechanically, hydraulically, or otherwise alter the configuration of the applicator to improve contact with the vessel wall or to expose selected regions of the applicator for treatment.

Within the tubular body, an ablation-medium supply line is provided for transporting the thermal medium to the treatment region. The supply line includes a plurality of spaced openings arranged along its length. These openings allow the ablation medium to exit the supply line at multiple locations, thereby distributing the medium more uniformly within the applicator or along the target tissue region. By spacing the openings in a selected pattern, the applicator can provide controlled thermal exposure over a defined treatment length, reducing the likelihood of uneven heating or cooling and improving the consistency of the ablation procedure.

The ablation medium may circulate through the applicator in a controlled flow path. After being delivered through the openings of the supply line, the medium can contact thermally conductive regions of the applicator and transfer heat to or from the surrounding vascular tissue. The medium may then be collected or redirected through a return pathway, allowing continued circulation during treatment. This circulating flow can help maintain a desired temperature profile and support a predictable ablation effect.

In some embodiments, the applicator includes an internal temperature sensor positioned within the tubular body. The temperature sensor can monitor the temperature of the ablation medium, the applicator wall, or a region associated with the treated tissue. Information from the sensor may be used by an external controller or treatment system to regulate medium temperature, flow rate, treatment duration, or other operating parameters. This feedback can improve procedural safety by helping prevent excessive thermal exposure and can enhance treatment efficacy by ensuring that the target tissue receives sufficient energy to achieve ablation.

The applicator may also include a shape-defining return line. In addition to providing a return path for the ablation medium, the return line may be configured to influence the shape or stiffness of the applicator. For example, the return line may be arranged so that, when actuated or pressurized, it causes the tubular body to bend, curve, expand, or otherwise assume a predetermined treatment configuration. This active shaping capability can help bring the applicator into closer thermal contact with the blood vessel tissue and can allow the physician to conform the device to the anatomy of the vessel being treated.

By combining a tubular applicator body, a controllable insertion and ablation mechanism, a distributed ablation-medium supply line, optional temperature sensing, and a shape-defining return line, the device enables more precise and controlled vascular tissue ablation. The arrangement promotes effective distribution of thermal medium, improves thermal contact with the target tissue, and allows the applicator shape and treatment conditions to be adjusted during use. As a result, the applicator can provide a predictable ablation zone while reducing the risk of unintended damage to adjacent tissue.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small and ordinary, but it plays an important role in the English language. It is called the definite article, and it helps point to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about one particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

“The” gives clarity and direction to a sentence. It helps readers and listeners know exactly what is being discussed. Whether we say “the sun,” “the city,” or “the answer,” this simple word makes communication more precise.

Although it is only three letters long, “the” is one of the most commonly used words in English. It appears in conversations, books, news articles, songs, and everyday messages. Its importance shows that even the smallest words can have a powerful effect on meaning.

In many ways, “the” reminds us that language depends not only on big, complex words, but also on simple ones that quietly hold sentences together.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for an ablation device applicator with a tubular body convertible between insertion and ablation configurations, where fluid openings along a supply tube thermally contact the tubular body.
counterfactuals.output:
An ablation device applicator includes an elongate tubular body configured for introduction into a patient in a low-profile insertion configuration and for conversion into an expanded or deployed ablation configuration at a treatment site. The tubular body may be formed from a flexible, compliant, or shape-memory material and may define an internal chamber or lumen through which a thermal ablation fluid is circulated.

A fluid supply tube extends within the tubular body and is configured to deliver heated or cooled ablation fluid into the tubular body. The supply tube includes a plurality of fluid openings arranged along at least a portion of its length. The openings may be spaced longitudinally and/or circumferentially so that fluid exiting the supply tube is distributed along the tubular body rather than discharged at only a distal end. In use, fluid passing through the openings directly contacts, impinges upon, or otherwise thermally communicates with an inner surface of the tubular body, thereby transferring thermal energy to the tubular body and to surrounding tissue.

The tubular body is convertible between configurations. In the insertion configuration, the tubular body may be collapsed, folded, radially compressed, or otherwise reduced in cross-sectional profile to facilitate advancement through a body passage, cannula, catheter, trocar, or surgical access tract. In the ablation configuration, the tubular body may expand, unfold, inflate, bow outward, or assume a predetermined shape to increase contact with target tissue. Expansion may be caused by pressure of the ablation fluid, mechanical actuation, release of an elastic or shape-memory structure, or a combination of these mechanisms.

During ablation, thermal fluid delivered through the supply tube exits the plurality of openings and flows into thermal contact with the tubular body. The fluid may heat or cool the tubular body substantially along the length of the opening pattern, creating a controlled ablation zone. The distributed openings promote more uniform temperature distribution, reduce localized hot or cold spots, and improve thermal coupling between the supply tube and the tubular body. Fluid may then be removed through a return lumen, an annular space between the supply tube and the tubular body, or one or more separate exhaust passages.

In some embodiments, the tubular body includes a heat-transfer wall configured to contact tissue when deployed. The wall may be thin enough to permit efficient thermal conduction while being sufficiently robust to contain the circulating fluid. The tubular body may include atraumatic ends, radiopaque markers, temperature sensors, pressure sensors, reinforcing elements, or insulation regions to shape or monitor the ablation profile.

The applicator may be used for thermal ablation of tissue by positioning the tubular body at a treatment site while in the insertion configuration, converting the tubular body to the ablation configuration, circulating thermal fluid through the supply tube openings so that the fluid thermally contacts the tubular body, maintaining treatment conditions for a selected duration, and then returning the tubular body to the insertion configuration for removal. The device may be suitable for cryoablation, heat ablation, endoluminal ablation, laparoscopic procedures, percutaneous procedures, or other applications requiring controlled delivery of thermal energy to tissue.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
